## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One critical defect must be fixed before merge: `preview` checks containment on the unresolved path. A relative path containing `..` passes that check, and the function then reads files outside the home directory. This review read `app/paths.py`, `tests/test_paths.py` and `tests/review-note.txt` in full. It traced how `Path.is_relative_to` handles `..` segments and symlinks. It did not run any tests. The added tests for the 200-character truncation and for `settings_file` match the code they exercise.

## Changes
The PR adds `preview(home, relative)` in `app/paths.py`, which returns the first 200 characters of a file under `home` and rejects paths outside it, plus `settings_file(home)`, which returns `home/settings.toml`. It also adds tests for both helpers and a one-line text file, `tests/review-note.txt`.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — Resolve paths before the outside-home check — Calling `preview(home, "../secret.txt")` returns the contents of a file outside `home` instead of raising `ValueError`. `Path(home) / "../secret.txt"` produces `home/../secret.txt`. `is_relative_to` compares path parts without resolving them, so it returns `True` because the path begins with `home`, and `read_text()` then opens the parent directory's file. A symlink inside `home` that points elsewhere passes the check the same way. — Any caller that passes a user-chosen relative path can read arbitrary files the process can access, which defeats the guard this function exists to provide. — Fix: Compare resolved paths, e.g. `base = Path(home).resolve(); candidate = (base / relative).resolve(); if not candidate.is_relative_to(base): raise ValueError(...)`. Also add test cases for `"../outside.txt"` and for a symlink inside `home`; the only rejection case in `tests/test_paths.py:20` uses an absolute path, which never exercises `..` traversal.
